questions.q: Bismillah Khan attained perfection in a very ________ time.
The flowing waters of the River ________ inspired him.

sections.passage: Bismillah Khan religiously practised the shehnai and attained perfection in a very short time. The flowing waters of the River Ganga inspired him to improvise and invent 'ragas' that were earlier considered to be beyond the range of shehnai. He often played the shehnai at the Vishwanath Temple on the banks of River Ganga.

sections.title: Answer in one or two sentences (about 30 words).

questions.q: How did Bismillah Khan get his name?
questions.answer: He was named Qamaruddin, but when his grandfather Rasool Baksh Khan saw him as a baby, he exclaimed 'Bismillah', and he came to be known as Bismillah Khan.

questions.q: How was Ali Baksh a source of inspiration for Bismillah Khan?
questions.answer: Ali Baksh, the official shehnai player at the Vishwanath Temple, noticed his keenness and taught him; Bismillah followed him all day and practised for hours under his guidance.

questions.q: What was the importance of the 1937 concert in Calcutta?
questions.answer: His concert at the All India Music Conference in Calcutta brought the shehnai into the limelight and was hugely appreciated by music lovers.

questions.q: What honour did Bismillah Khan have on the eve of Independence?
questions.answer: He played the shehnai at the Red Fort in Delhi on the eve of Independence in 1947, and afterwards every year on 15 August after the Prime Minister's speech.

questions.q: How was Bismillah Khan honoured at his death?
questions.answer: The Government declared a day of national mourning, and he was buried with his shehnai under a neem tree in Varanasi with a 21-gun salute from the Indian Army.

questions.q: How do we know that Bismillah Khan remained simple even after becoming famous?
questions.answer: He never accumulated wealth or material possessions, lived in humble surroundings in Varanasi, used a cycle rickshaw as his favourite transport, and declined an offer of permanent US citizenship out of love for his city and country.

or.q: What was Bismillah Khan's contribution to music and to national unity?
or.answer: He made the shehnai famous and brought it into mainstream classical music, invented new ragas, and kept the legacy of classical music alive through his recitals. He believed in Hindu-Muslim unity, played at the Vishwanath Temple and often said 'Music has no caste', spreading brotherhood through music.
